subject: RFI: Phased onboarding, validation & fallback plan for CloudBank deployment
messages:
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@cloudbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudBank Procurement <procurement@cloudbank.com>, Tom Herrera <tom.herrera@cloudbank.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Implementation plan details and fallback validation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. Procurement has asked for a more granular RFI response focused on the actual implementation/migration steps, canary strategy, validation gates, and fallback/rollback controls.

High-level asks from CloudBank:
- Phased onboarding timeline by environment (dev, staging, prod) with milestone owners and SLA targets for each phase
- Integration steps for identity (SAML/OIDC), KMS key wrapping, and log forwarding to our SIEM
- Canary release plan with percent traffic, validation metrics, and automatic rollback criteria
- Data migration approach for historic embeddings and KV caches (estimated size ~1.2TB)
- Runbook snippets for a failed rolling upgrade and emergency failover

Can you respond with a document and a one-page timeline matrix by COB Tuesday (Nov 2)? Procurement will use this to score the implementation risk.

Also please include any required customer responsibilities (network changes, peering, firewall IPs) so we can coordinate.

Regards,
Alice Wong
Director, Technical Sourcing
CloudBank

[Attachment: CloudBank_RFI_AppendixA.pdf (PDF reference)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@cloudbank.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Implementation plan details and fallback validation

Alice —

Thanks, helpful list. We're attaching a formal RFI response and a matrix (see attachments) that maps the phases, validation gates, and customer responsibilities. Below are the short answers and the ask for a technical deep-dive Thursday if that works.

Quick summary (detailed doc attached):
- Timeline: 3 phases over 12 weeks (Pilot: 2w, Staging rollout: 4w, Production graduation: 6w). Milestones and owners in sheet.
- Identity: SAML 2.0 with IdP-initiated and SP-initiated modes supported; we recommend OIDC for programmatic workloads.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or external HSM; envelope encryption and key rotation policies documented in appendix.
- Canary: Automated traffic shifting via our routing plane — typical start 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 24–48h windows. Canary health metrics = 99th pct latency, error rate, token-cost delta, and quality regression (prompt set).
- Data migration: We recommend a hybrid incremental bulk load for embeddings (S3 -> our staging nodes) followed by live sync; for KV caches we seed prefix caches and warm with replay traffic.
- Rollback: Auto-fallback to previous model variant and region failover within <5m for traffic reroute; we provide runbooks.

Can Stephanie and Markus weigh in on the migration steps and KMS notes in the attached?

Proposed next steps:
1) We upload the formal response (attached) into your portal today.
2) Technical deep-dive with engineering Thurs 11/4 10:00–11:00 PT — proposes: Stephanie, Markus, Lauren, Tom (CloudBank), Alice.
3) Agree on customer prep tasks (VPN/IPs, service-account roles, SAML metadata).

Best,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: CLDBK-RFI-Implementation-Responses-v1.docx, CLDBK-Phased-Onboarding-Timeline.xlsx]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Alice Wong <alice.wong@cloudbank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Tom Herrera <tom.herrera@cloudbank.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Implementation plan details and fallback validation

Thanks — adding technical detail inline for procurement scoring. See also attached KMS notes.

-----Pilot (Week 0–2)-----
Objectives: establish connectivity, basic identity assertions, and a lightweight PD/POC workload (10k tokens/day).
Steps:
1) Network & Access (Day 0–2)
   - Customer: open egress to our IP ranges (appendix), provision service account with scoped IAM roles, provide SAML metadata.
   - Redwood: create tenant, publish service endpoints, share SAML SP metadata.
2) KMS Integration (Day 1–4)
   - For AWS KMS: customer shares CMK ARN with cross-account IAM role. We perform envelope encryption; CMK never leaves customer account.
   - For HSM: provide mTLS endpoint and key-wrapping protocol details.
3) Data seeding (Day 2–5)
   - Customer uploads historic embedding tarballs to an S3 bucket with temporary cross-account role. Redwood performs an incremental import to staging nodes. Estimated throughput ~300GB/day; full 1.2TB load ~4–5 days.
4) Validation (Day 6–14)
   - Run 3 canonical prompt sets (accuracy/regression), measure latency & token-cost metrics, and confirm logs are flowing to customer SIEM via our forwarding connector (syslog/HTTPS).

-----Staging rollout (Week 3–6)-----
Objectives: expanded traffic, canary gating, automation of CI/CD for model variants.
Steps:
- Canary plan: start at 1% traffic for 6h: monitor 99th pct latency, 5xx error rate, model-quality score delta. If all pass for 24h, shift to 5%. After 48h at 5% with green metrics, shift to 20% and run for 72h. Failure at any gate triggers immediate rollback to previous variant and an alert to both teams.
- Observability: integrate tracing headers (x-request-id), token-level cost reports, and per-route dashboards preconfigured for CloudBank routes.

-----Production graduation (Week 7–12)-----
Objectives: full capacity, autoscale policies, SLA handoff.
Steps:
- Performance tuning: kernel-selection profiles and batching policies tuned to CloudBank seqLen distribution.
- Autoscaling: define baseline throughput and burst buffer; Redwood Dedicated pool reserved for CloudBank.
- Rollout: automated blue/green plus regional fallback. In regional outage, traffic reroutes to secondary region; pilot failover test scheduled in Week 10.

-----Rollback & Emergency runbook (snippet)-----
- Trigger: >0.5% 5xx over 15m OR 20% quality regression on sentinel prompt set.
- Action: automatic traffic shift to previous model variant (control-plane action), optional region failover. Post-mortem within 24h.

Customer responsibilities (summary):
- Provide SAML metadata and service accounts prior to Day 0.
- Open IP egress and provision S3 or storage for bulk import.
- Schedule a 2-hour maintenance window for KV cache seeding during Week 2.

Attachments: redwood_kms_integration_notes.pdf (KMS steps & IAM policy examples)

Happy to expand any section for procurement scoring.

-Stephanie
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Herrera <tom.herrera@cloudbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Wong <alice.wong@cloudbank.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 12:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Implementation plan details and fallback validation

Appreciate the level of detail. Two follow-ups from the security team:
1) Can you confirm whether audit logs (request-level metadata and decisions) can be forwarded to our Splunk instance in UTC with HMAC verification?
2) For KMS/HSM, we need an explicit description of key rotation impact on active sessions — will existing in-flight tokens continue to be decrypted if CMK is rotated?

Also procurement wants the explicit list of IP ranges for Week 0 firewall rules (we need CIDR blocks).

If you can answer those three items inline we can mark this RFI as low-risk.

-Tom
CloudBank Security

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Herrera <tom.herrera@cloudbank.com>, Alice Wong <alice.wong@cloudbank.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Implementation plan details and fallback validation

Tom —

Answers inline:
1) Audit logs: yes — we can forward request-level metadata to Splunk over HTTPS with optional HMAC header for integrity. We also support syslog/forwarder agents. Timestamps are emitted in UTC; we can include an HMAC per-batch and nightly checksum if you require tamper-evidence.
2) Key rotation: envelope-encryption design means existing ciphertext (encrypted with older data keys) remains decryptable; during CMK rotation we derive a new data key but we keep the previous key available for decrypting in-flight or pre-existing data for a configurable grace period (default 30 days). Live requests are not interrupted, and we publish rotation windows in the control plane. Stephanie: we included the exact policy in redwood_kms_integration_notes.pdf.
3) IP ranges: see appendix A of the timeline sheet — primary egress CIDRs: 34.201.12.0/24, 54.152.33.0/24, and 18.204.45.0/24. We'll provide a signed CSV for procurement to ingest.

Next steps: I'll upload the signed RFI package to your portal and confirm the Thurs 11/4 deep-dive. If procurement gets low-risk signoff from security, we can move to contract redlines.

Thanks all,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
